# CodeQL cancels the analysis of a superseded pull request head

## Context

Split from #21541's AC-2 at that ticket's author's request (intake: issuecomment-7047158369). The organisation's 20 runners are shared by every repository, and #21541 measured PR jobs waiting 5–16 minutes for one. Peers already cancel superseded runs by hand to free slots (Memory Core, 2026-11-05).

## The Problem

`codeql-analysis.yml` has no `concurrency` group. Receipt: at `origin/dev` `29d90a1c23` it has 0 `concurrency:` lines, against 1 in `test.yml` as a positive control. A push that supersedes a pull request's head leaves the older head's analysis running to completion, on a runner the queue needs, for a result nobody reads.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: "No concurrency group: `edited` re-runs this guard on an unchanged head, and a cancelled sibling run stays red in that head's rollup for good (`#20064`)." (`.github/workflows/file-size-guard.yml:20-21`)

- That constraint is about cancelling a run on the SAME head. CodeQL's `pull_request` trigger uses the default activity types (`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`) with no `edited`, so a run cancelled on `synchronize` always belongs to a superseded head.
- `reopened` can start a second run on an unchanged head, so it must queue behind the first rather than cancel it.
- `push` to `dev` and `schedule` runs must never cancel each other: a cancelled `dev` push leaves its own diff unexamined (the class of `#20363`).
- In-repo precedent for the group shape: `test.yml` and `test-e2e.yml` key a group per run, falling back to `github.run_id` for re-runs.

## The Fix

Add to `.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml`:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: codeql-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.run_attempt == '1' && github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}
```

The group is keyed on the pull request, not the ref. Only a new head cancels; `push`, `schedule` and re-runs get a group of their own.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A push that supersedes a pull request's head cancels the older head's CodeQL run, and the new head's run completes (receipt: run ids from two consecutive pushes on one PR).
- [ ] AC-2: `dev` pushes, scheduled runs, re-runs and a `reopened` run never cancel another CodeQL run (receipt: the group expression, plus one `dev` push run after merge).

## Out of Scope

- File Size Guard keeps no concurrency group (`#20064`); folding it is #21504.
- Saturation-aware shard planning (#21541's Fix 2, a design question).
- Other workflows, which already cancel superseded runs.

## Avoided Traps

- Keying the group on `github.ref` for every event would let successive `dev` pushes cancel each other's analysis (`#20363`).
- Cancelling on `reopened` or `edited` would leave a cancelled sibling red on an unchanged head (`#20064`).
